Controls and electronics · NNSA Compact Accelerator Project

Advanced accelerator technology. Purpose-built controls.

BL Monitor and Control develops control systems and electronics for demanding scientific applications. As a subcontractor to Fermilab, we support the NNSA Compact Accelerator Project with the instrumentation, interfaces and controls needed to bring a cutting-edge accelerator to life.

The project

Making powerful accelerators more practical

At Fermilab’s Illinois Accelerator Research Center (IARC), the NNSA Compact Accelerator Project is developing a compact superconducting radio-frequency electron accelerator for potential industrial applications.

The project is a technology demonstrator intended to help transfer compact accelerator technology to industry. Its design combines superconducting acceleration with commercial cryocoolers, aiming to deliver high beam power without a conventional liquid-helium bath.

Potential applications include X-ray generation for medical-device sterilization.

650 MHz RF frequency
1.6 MeV Target beam energy
20 kW Target beam power

Our contribution

Connecting the equipment behind the accelerator

A compact accelerator brings together sensitive RF, cryogenic, vacuum and instrumentation systems. Our work focuses on the controls and electronics that help the team monitor, test and coordinate these subsystems as the project develops.

Hardware interfaces

Connect pumps, coolers, sensors and other equipment to a common control environment.

Instrumentation

Acquire the temperatures, pressures, flows and status signals needed to understand system behavior.

Low-level RF

Support precise control and monitoring of the superconducting cavity’s RF system.

Machine protection

Monitor configured alarm conditions, coordinate protective actions and record events for analysis.

Web-based controls

Bring operational information and subsystem interfaces together in a web-based environment.

Designed for the field

From laboratory demonstration to industrial operation

The project’s goal of transferring accelerator technology to industry changes the requirements for its control system. An accelerator deployed in the field may not have a national laboratory’s large on-site team of control engineers and technical specialists.

Operators need a practical way to monitor equipment, respond to issues and connect with experts when support is needed.

BL Monitor and Control’s Blinky-Lite™ platform was selected for this application with those needs in mind. It brings subsystem interfaces, instrumentation, alarms and web-based monitoring together in a platform designed for distributed equipment and secure remote access.

Why Blinky-Lite™

Built for equipment beyond the lab

Remote expertise. Secure remote access helps qualified specialists monitor and troubleshoot equipment without always being on site.

Event-driven communication. Publish-subscribe messaging distributes updates as they occur, supporting timely notification and coordination across subsystems.

Intelligence close to the equipment. Edge computing places control functions near the devices they serve.

A system that grows with the project. Modular interfaces and software allow controls to be introduced during component testing and expanded as the accelerator develops.

Engineering capabilities

From prototype electronics to integrated systems

Scientific equipment often combines specialized hardware with components from multiple manufacturers. We bridge those interfaces, developing electronics and software that help engineers test components and build toward an integrated system.

Our work on this project spans hardware integration, instrumentation, RF controls, automation and operational interfaces—capabilities applicable to complex research and industrial equipment.

In development

A test stand for critical technologies

The project’s test stand brings together a superconducting cavity, vacuum and cooling systems, instrumentation, RF controls and machine protection.

It gives the team a way to evaluate components and their integration during development.
